title: Checkpoint 3 — Reading the Room (DHT22)
description: Quick check after Build #2: wiring and reading the DHT22 sensor.

questions.prompt: Which GPIO pin do we connect the DHT22's DATA line to?
questions.explanation: DATA goes to GPIO 4; VCC goes to 3V3 and GND goes to GND.

questions.prompt: Why does the bare DHT22 need a 10 kΩ pull-up resistor on its DATA line?
choices: The sensor has no built-in pull-up, so it keeps the data signal clean
It doesn't — the resistor is just decoration
questions.explanation: Without the pull-up holding the line HIGH, the readings come back garbled (often NaN).

questions.prompt: What does dht.readHumidity() give you back?
questions.explanation: readHumidity() returns % relative humidity; readTemperature() returns °C.

questions.prompt: Your code prints NaN instead of a number. What does that usually mean?
choices: The sensor read failed — check the wiring and pull-up resistor
questions.explanation: NaN = 'not a number'. 99% of the time it's a loose wire, wrong pin, or missing pull-up.

questions.prompt: What happens to the humidity reading when you breathe on the DHT22?
questions.explanation: Your breath is humid, so the number spikes instantly — great for testing it works!
